final.title: When redaction becomes a workflow decision
final.body:
If you keep redacting the same names, IDs, or fields over and over, the question is not whether AI is clever enough. It is whether this is still a one-off habit or a repeatable workflow.

For a small business owner, that distinction matters. A single redaction can stay manual. A recurring pattern inside digital documents or SaaS tools starts to look like a workflow decision: identify one pattern, decide whether it happens often enough to deserve a bounded review, and keep the owner in charge of the final call.

A simple test is this: are you redacting the same fields weekly or more often, and is it pulling you away from revenue work or lead follow-up? If not, keep it manual. If yes, define the narrowest possible workflow and review the output before anything is sent or stored.

Bareni currently treats high-sensitivity legal, medical, and financial work as out of scope. That is current scope discipline, not a claim that such work can never be automated.

The practical next step is plain: note what gets redacted, how often it happens, and which tool it lives in. If the pattern is boring and recurring, it is worth looking at as a workflow. If it is rare, manual is probably fine.
